properties.answer: Approved (Anthony, 2026-07-25). Prove the nudge path end to end in a real session and give it a backstop for when it is absent. The fleet's rule stands behind this: a mechanism you rely on to interrupt you is worthless until you have observed it interrupt you — they banned two plausible implementations by name after measuring zero wakes.
properties.context_setter: Nothing satisfies requirement “The path the coherence loop relies on to interrupt an agent is proven to interrupt one”
properties.question: reflow2 relies on a reminder that taps the assistant on the shoulder when design work has gone unchecked — but nothing has ever proved that tap actually lands in a real session, and there is no fallback if it does not. Is proving it worth the work, given that everything reflow2 does to keep itself honest depends on it arriving?
